items.name: Chapter 13, Evidence and sourcing

reasons.craft: The mapping table’s rules now run whole, the cards sit centered at true size, 13.7 and 13.13 draw through the kit, and patterned lines run solid under their ticks, though the opener sets a numeral inside a quotation (R1).
reasons.clarity: The intro is 73 words and the opener’s grade chip and first typed chip reach the first screen at 1440 px, and the terms I checked (Supplemental Poverty Measure, seasonally adjusted, feasibility, pharmacy benefit managers) are defined at first use.
reasons.brand_fidelity: The opener now carries the evidence chip on the first screen, the line code holds at 2x, and red appears only as Rule 12.5’s target in 13.5, one meaning per view.
reasons.usefulness: Rule 13.4 cites the ten oa.chart.grade tokens by name with their values, which match tokens.json (shortest run 20 widths, 1 px rails, 28 px lead-in), and Rule 13.1 says what a diagram prints in the label’s place.
reasons.evidence_honesty: No plate prints “Official statistic”, 13.9 reads “can raise”, atlas names sit in quotation marks, 13.7 names both groups and one release, and 13.1 prints its margin of error and its estimate’s method, though 13.2’s Documented title states a fact other than its connection’s claim (R2).
reasons.accessibility: Grade travels in pattern, word and the record square, and the phone tables stack readably at 390 px; I did not rerun axe or read the new alt texts, and the editor reports 0 axe violations at both widths.

pending.name: The chart kit with S01 to S16
pending.status: Rescored when the engineer’s last items land and the main session sends the build

R1.what: Numeral 1 sits inside the quoted atlas name, “Political spending can ❶ tilt policy toward donors”, so a mark breaks a quotation Rule 13.12 asks to print exactly.
R1.fix: Set the numeral after the closing quotation mark, or before the title with the list naming the verb “can”.

R2.what: The other four rows title the connection’s own claim at its grade. The Documented row’s title, “The Department of Transportation had spent 46.6 percent of the infrastructure law’s transportation funds by July 31, 2026”, states a fact from the record’s evidence, while Connection LE02 claims “Congress decides public investment levels”.
R2.fix: Title the claim in record words, such as “Congress set the infrastructure law’s investment levels in 2021”, and keep the spending figure in the source line.

R3.what: The data lead asks the creative director to choose. In the light-fill variant the named bar stands apart in gray (0.371 against 0.635) and every value prints beside its bar; in view 1 it prints almost like its neighbors (0.371 against 0.386).
R3.fix: Adopt the light fill for the other bars wherever one named bar is emphasized, in red or in ink, and write it into chapter 14’s palette specification in round 5.

risks_for_dustin: Chapter 13 builds at 248,530 bytes of its 250,000 ceiling. Any later word or plate change will pass the ceiling; the editor should cut before adding, and the engineer’s weight pass may free room.
The two new colors, Prussian 56 and 29 percent toward Newsprint, still wait for Dustin’s approval on board 1. I recommend he approve them.
